assertions.name: exponent_is_minus_one_half_on_tightest_pair
assertions.source: the 4_1/L5a1 two-point determination gives p = -1/2 to better than 1e-15. NOT independent evidence: algebraically identical to the published k_1 = k_2, and asserted here only so the re-expression is machine-checked rather than asserted

assertions.name: free_fit_recovers_minus_one_half
assertions.source: least squares over all four manifolds, p free, lands within 1e-2 of -1/2 across ~1 decade of |tau|

description: Measures the exponent p in the prefactor form c_sigma = k*|tau|^p instead of assuming it. Every prior check in this arc computes k_c = c_sigma*|tau|^(1/2) and tests its constancy, which has p = -1/2 substituted in and so cannot see the exponent at all. Here p is free and -1/2 is a prediction. Four manifolds whose c_sigma is determined INDEPENDENTLY of tau (three from colored Jones asymptotics, 5_2 from Ohtsuki's Theorem 1.1), spanning ~1 decade in |tau|. Splits the single assumption recorded in the c_sigma derivation status audit into two, of which only one — that c_sigma depends on tau alone — is still assumed. Derives nothing new; nothing wired.

4_1.c_sigma_provenance: colored Jones asymptotic (van der Veen exact + Neville), 17 digits

5_2.c_sigma_provenance: Ohtsuki Thm 1.1 |omega|, a rigorous theorem, 10 printed digits

data.independence_of_inputs: c_sigma and tau must be measured independently or the test is circular. 4_1 / L5a1 / L6a4 take c_sigma from the colored Jones asymptotic (pure mpmath, exact colored Jones, no SnapPy and no determinant); 5_2 takes it from Ohtsuki's theorem. tau_DG is computed from the geometry in every case. In particular the L5a1 value used here is the 20-digit MEASURED c_sigma, NOT the 2^(-3/4) predicted by the form under test.

tightest_determination.NOT_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE: k_i = k_j and p_ij = -1/2 are algebraically the same statement, so this re-expresses the already-published k_1 = k_2 (rel diff 4.5e-18) rather than confirming it again. Recorded because the re-expression is the finding — it shows the exponent was pinned by data the corpus already had — not because it is new evidence.
tightest_determination.why: the c=1 and c=2 anchors the derivation turns on, and the two whose c_sigma carry the most digits

data.what_is_still_assumed: That c_sigma is a function of tau ALONE. A law c_sigma = k*|tau|^p*f(M) with f weakly varying across these four manifolds fits equally well and is not excluded by any data here. The EXPONENT is not the assumed part and never was — pairwise, it is the same statement as the k-constancy the corpus already measured. The functional dependence, and the universality of k across cusp number, are what carry the weight.
data.scope: measures an exponent. Proves no form. Adds no manifold and no link beyond those already in the corpus, so it says nothing new about c-dependence. The L6a4 residual is not evidence against p = -1/2: that tower carries a documented normalisation+cusp offset flagged in its own witness.
